question.text: Theodora may have influenced her husband to include women's rights in this legal code that is contained within the Corpus Juris Civilis . This legal code was created to specify the laws of the Byzantine Empire under its namesake emperor.
question.clue: This work contains strikingly accurate transcription of quotes by Gaius and includes several writings by Ulpian as part of the Pandects, or Digest.

swap.text: The Byzantine capital was this city, which was renamed Istanbul after it fell to the Ottomans.
swap.clue: Attacks on Damascus and Baghdad by Tamerlane led Bayezid the Thunderbolt to pull out of a siege of this city.

question.text: Justinian was a ruler of this empire, which survived as the eastern half of the Roman Empire.
question.clue: The target of the Fourth Crusade, in 1453 this empire fell after its capital was sacked by Turkish forces in 1453.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the general Belisarius.
swap.text: Belisarius spearheaded the reconquest of Ostrogothic Italy under this Byzantine Emperor, who was denoted "the Great." He is best known for his namesake legal code, which revised and clarified centuries of previous Roman law.
swap.answerHtml: Justinian I [or Justinian the Great or Flavius Petrus Sabbatius Iustinianus Augustus]
swap.clue: Peter Barsymes collected taxes under this ruler, who is accused of killing a myriad myriad of myriads and of being a demon who can make his head disappear in the Secret History of Procopius .

question.leadin: Procopius described this building as looking "as though it were suspended from heaven by [a] golden chain."
question.text: Name this former church constructed under Justinian that was later converted to a Mosque in 1453 during the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople.
question.answerHtml: Hagia Sophia [or Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque or Church of God’s Holy Wisdom]
question.clue: On its southwestern entrance of this building is a mosaic of two important emperors presenting models of this building and its city to the Virgin Mary.

swap.leadin: This Byzantine general's last victory came in 559 A.D. when he defeated a force of Huns and Slavs outside of Constantinople.
swap.text: Name this general who conquered the Vandal kingdom in Africa at the Battle of Tricameron and who went on to fight and conquer most of the Ostrogothic kingdom of Italy.
swap.clue: He was ordered to depose Pope Silverius in favor of Vigilius, an act for which he later repented, and he married Antonina, a court favorite who wielded a good deal of influence.

question.leadin: Description acceptable. Isidore of Kiev apocryphally survived this event by dressing up a dead body with his clothes so that it would be beheaded instead of him.
question.text: Name this event for which the engineer Orban designed a cannon known as "The Basilic" to destroy the Theodosian Walls.
question.answerHtml: Fall of Constantinople [accept answers generally describing a Siege of Constantinople; accept BUT DO NOT REVEAL answers indicating that Constantinople being is captured by the Ottomans; accept the end of the Byzantine Empire]
question.clue: Giovanni Giustiniani ordered his ships to defend the Golden Horn during this event, which also saw which saw one side utilize Orban's "Basilica" cannons.

swap.text: A supporter of the Blues, this Byzantine emperor was nearly overthrown in the Nika riots. He promulgated a legal code and his queen was Theodora.
swap.clue: This major Byzantine emperor codified Roman law with his namesake law code and sent his general Belisarius to reconquer Italy from barbarian tribes which had overrun the Roman empire

question.text: Funded by Venice, this crusade looted Constantinople in 1204 and gave up on reaching the Middle East.
question.clue: Pope Innocent III excommunicated all of its participants when they attacked the Dalmatian capital in exchange for assistance from Enrico Dandolo, the doge of Venice.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the wonderful world of wartime weaponry.
swap.text: This Byzantine ruler was described as inventing several types of trebuchets during the 1097 Siege of Nicaea. This ruler's request of aid from Europe triggered the First Crusade, and his daughter Anna wrote a notable biography of him.
swap.clue: Although one rival was forced to give up his territorial gains to assist Henry IV, that rival, Robert Guiscard, defeated this man's forces at the Battle of Dyrrachium.

question.leadin: Decisive victories at the battles of Ad Decimum and Tricamarum allowed this general to conquer North Africa.
question.text: Name this general whose numerous victories and conquests against the Goths, Vandals, and Persians fueled a ruler's desire to regain an old empire.
question.clue: Early in this leader's career, together with Mundus they were instrumental in ensuring Hypatius and Pompeius did not take the throne.

swap.text: The Council of Clermont was ostensibly called to assist this embattled Byzantine emperor, who did not ask for a full-scale invasion of the Holy Land. Still, he took advantage of the Crusade to regain lost territory in Anatolia.
swap.clue: The insane monk Raiktor joined a force against this man that won the Battle of Dyrrhachium and Robert Guiscard.

question.text: The most famous member of this family temporarily ended the Great Schism with the Second Council of Lyon after reclaiming Constantinople from the Latin Empire. That man, Michael VIII, established this family as the final Byzantine dynasty.
question.clue: Michael VIII founded this dynasty, which expelled the Crusaders from Constantinople in 1261 and were the last to rule Byzantium before the Turkish conquest in 1453.

swap.text: This elite group of Norse fighters in the Byzantine army was formed when Basil the Bulgar-Slayer had his sister Anna married off to Vladimir the Great in exchange for their service.
swap.clue: As punishment for replacing this group with loyal Scythians, Michael V ("the fifth") was castrated and blinded by Harald Hardrada.

question.text: The Isaurians were known for this policy that was most forcefully promulgated by Constantine V and formally sanctioned at the Council of Hieria. It was influenced by the Muslim custom of not depicting living things in sacred spaces, and prompted some enthusiastic destruction sprees.
question.clue: This practice was carried out by mobs during the Dissolution of the Monasteries and again by the Puritans.

swap.text: Some people believe that Hereward fled to the employ of the fifth Count of Flanders to bear this name, which he shared with two Kings of Jerusalem who followed Godrey of Bouillon and reigned from 1100 to 1131.
swap.clue: This cousin of Rudyard Kipling highlighted the power of aerial attacks by noting that "the bomber will always get through."

question.leadin: The Arvanites under Peter Bua rose up in revolt in this principality in the 15th century.
question.text: Name this principality in the Peloponnese that was first ruled over by Manuel Kantakouzenos in 1349. Along with Epirus, the despot of this region was usually a son of the Byzantine Emperor.

swap.text: The second ruler of this dynasty, Leo VI the Wise, prescribed harsh punishments for counterfeiting alchemists in his Book of the Eparch. Leo completed the Basilika law code named after the founder of this dynasty, Basil I.
swap.clue: Chief military figures from this period include Nicephorus Phocas and an Armenian usurper, John Tzimisces, though its most notable battlefield accomplishment may have come against the army of Tsar Samuel.

question.leadin: This ruler, who introduced jousting and other Western European traditions to his kingdom, was hailed as a chivalric model by contemporaries, such as his chronicler John Kinnamos.
question.text: Identify this grandson of Alexius I, a Byzantine emperor who attempted an alliance with the papacy under Adrian IV. His attempt to regain Anatolia was halted at the Battle of Myriokephalon.
question.clue: While this ruler's armies besieged the island of Corfu, the Venetians mocked this ruler by having an African slave impersonate him.

swap.leadin: This clash took place near modern-day Konya, and the victory of the winning side is generally attributed to their ability to occupy the elevated position.
swap.text: Identify this 1176 battle in which the forces of the Sultanate of Rum, led by Arslan II, inflicted an overwhelming defeat on the Byzantine army.
